_what: Backbone go/no-go probes. A backbone row costs ~140 GPU-hours; these are the cheap measurements that decide whether that spend can produce a row at all.
_two_axes: A validation score says whether we can MEASURE a backbone. The training-set group pass rate (scripts/phase3_port_model.py passrate) says whether it can LEARN. They are different questions and the second one is the gate.

llama_base_eval.protocol: run/eval_steerf.sh with trainer.val_only=True, H200 x1, gpu_memory_utilization 0.8, tp 1
llama_base_eval.source: session transcript -- the eval log is not in git
llama_base_eval._reward_note: verl/utils/reward_score/multi_datasets_eval.py:327 scores (dapo_correct OR qwen_correct), so dapo_correct = 0 is not itself fatal -- qwen_correct carries the accuracy and -0.96 is exactly 0.02*1 + 0.98*(-1). The grader is fine; the solve rate is 2%.
llama_base_eval._cause: The base tokenizer ships a chat template, and both scripts/_common.py:221 and verl's RLHFDataset apply a template when one is present, so a model that was never instruction-tuned is handed the instruction format. It continues the prompt instead of answering it.
llama_base_eval._verdict: no-go. At a 2% solve rate .98^8 = .85 of the GRPO groups come back all-wrong and contribute zero advantage.

passrate._how: python3 scripts/phase3_port_model.py passrate --model <path> --prompts datasets/DAPO-Math-17k.parquet --n-prompts 200 --group-size 8 --out <file>, then paste the summary here. Absolute values are not reward rates -- that tool grades with phase1_validate.answers_match, not the training reward -- so only the ratio against the reference backbone means anything.
